Same date-driven Status derivation as accreditation: Active / Expired / Future from valid_from..valid_to.
steps: openemis_get('institution-registrations', params: {institution_id: <id>, _fields: ['id','institution_id','valid_from','valid_to'], orderby: 'valid_from', order: 'desc'})
Compute Status per row: Active = valid_from <= today AND (valid_to null OR today <= valid_to); Expired = today > valid_to; Future = today < valid_from.
Identify the current registration (Status=Active) and report its valid_to as the next renewal deadline (or note 'open-ended' if valid_to is null).
If no Active row exists, surface a warning — the institution is currently unregistered for at least part of today.
notes: Same permissions model as institution-accreditations: read open to roles 1-7,9,10; write restricted to roles with order < 5.
Registration history is NOT user-deletable from the UI (HideButton). If the user asks 'remove a registration row', they have to use the API directly — and that requires write permission.

playbooks.title: View institution budget records (Core 5.10.0)
playbooks.description: List the budget records attached to an institution and resolve their budget types and academic periods. Useful for the question 'what budget did the school plan for this year?' or 'show me last year's budget vs this year's.'
schema_invariants: institution_budgets columns: id, institution_id, academic_period_id, budget_type_id, amount, file_name, file_content (longblob — do NOT request this field unless the user wants the file), description, modified_user_id/modified, created_user_id/created.
amount is a string in the API response (CakePHP decimal handling) — parseFloat before summing.
file_content is the attachment binary. Always exclude it from list responses via _fields to keep payloads small. Fetch by id when the user wants the actual file.
steps: openemis_get('institution-budgets', params: {institution_id: <id>, academic_period_id: <period>, _fields: ['id','academic_period_id','budget_type_id','amount','description','created'], limit: 100})
openemis_get('budget-types', params: {_fields: ['id','name'], limit: 50}) — global reference list, cache it.
If filtering across years, also fetch academic-periods to humanize period labels.
Sum amount per budget_type_id to answer 'total operating budget' / 'total capital budget' style questions.
If the user wants the attachment, do a single-row GET on institution-budgets/{id} requesting _fields=['file_name','file_content'] — but warn them the response will be large.

playbooks.title: Query a student's absence history (Core 5.10.0 aggregates)
playbooks.description: Answer 'how often was this student absent last term?' / 'what days did they miss?' / 'are absences clustering?'. Core 5.10.0 exposes two aggregate resources: institution-student-absences (per-day rows with absence_type_id) and institution-student-absence-days (multi-day spans with absent_days count). They complement the per-period student-attendance-marked-records used during roll call.
schema_invariants: institution-student-absences is a flat per-day record: id, student_id, institution_id, academic_period_id, institution_class_id, education_grade_id, date, absence_type_id, institution_student_absence_day_id (FK back to the span row).

institution-student-absence-days collapses consecutive days into a span: id, student_id, institution_id, absence_type_id, absent_days (integer), start_date, end_date. Use it for 'longest absence stretch' questions.
absence_type_id resolves via the absence-types reference list. 1 typically = Unexcused, 2 = Excused, but ALWAYS resolve names — sites can edit them.

An absence in institution-student-absences does NOT imply a row in student-attendance-marked-records (and vice versa). The per-period roll-call records and the per-day aggregates are independent surfaces — joining them is application-level glue, not a DB FK.
steps: Resolve the academic period(s) of interest: openemis_get('academic-periods', params: {_fields: ['id','code','name','start_date','end_date'], limit: 50})

List per-day absences: openemis_get('institution-student-absences', params: {student_id: <id>, academic_period_id: <period>, _fields: ['date','absence_type_id','institution_class_id'], limit: 365, orderby: 'date', order: 'desc'})

List span aggregates: openemis_get('institution-student-absence-days', params: {student_id: <id>, _fields: ['absence_type_id','absent_days','start_date','end_date'], orderby: 'start_date', order: 'desc'})
Resolve absence_type_id → human label: openemis_get('absence-types', params: {_fields: ['id','name','code'], limit: 50})

Render: total absent days for the period (sum of absent_days from the span table — that's the canonical count, not the per-day rows), broken down by type. Flag if any single span >= 5 consecutive days (chronic-absence threshold the ministry typically cares about).
notes: POCOR-9560/9660 deprecated some legacy attendance paths — the v4 student-attendances endpoints are gone. Stick to v5 only.
Do not try to derive the span table from the per-day table — the span table is the source of truth for absent_days. Per-day rows are for surfacing exception days; the span row aggregates them.
If you need the reason free-text (e.g. 'sick — doctor's note attached'), fetch institution-student-absence-details linked by composite key. Most playbook callers won't need that depth.

playbooks.title: Query the user activity audit log (POCOR-9697 — Wave 3)
playbooks.description: Answer 'who changed this record?' / 'when was this user's password reset?' / 'show all writes by user X this week.' POCOR-9697 (Core 5.10.0) introduced Wave-3 audit logging: every write through the v5 API is recorded into user_activities with per-field old/new snapshots, redacted for sensitive columns. The CakePHP stack writes the same row shape via a ported trait.
schema_invariants: user_activities row shape: id, model (PHP class like 'Institutions'), model_reference (the row's PK as a string), field (column name), field_type, old_value, new_value, operation (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), security_user_id (actor — derived from JWT, never client-supplied), created_user_id, created.

On DELETE: per-field snapshot is taken BEFORE the row is removed, so the audit captures the entire deleted row. The FK to security_users is ON DELETE SET NULL — hard-deleting a user keeps the audit but loses the actor link.

Redactions: password, super_admin, and photo_content fields are never written to user_activities. If you see a UPDATE row on security_users with no 'password' field, that's the redaction at work — not a missing entry.

The actor (security_user_id) is ALWAYS the JWT subject. It is NOT trusted from request body — POCOR-9697 explicitly strips client-supplied created_user_id/modified_user_id on the read side and derives them server-side.
steps: openemis_get('user-activities', params: {security_user_id: <actor_id>, _fields: ['model','model_reference','field','old_value','new_value','operation','created'], orderby: 'created', order: 'desc', limit: 200}) — 'what did this user change recently?'
openemis_get('user-activities', params: {model: 'Institutions', model_reference: '<institution_id>', orderby: 'created', order: 'desc'}) — 'what was changed on this institution row?'
To time-bound: add _conditions=created>=<iso-date> and created<=<iso-date>. The created column is a DATETIME and indexed.
For DELETE diagnostics: filter operation='DELETE' and the rows give you a full per-field snapshot of what was removed — useful for restore work.
Resolve security_user_id → username via security-users (limit lookups; cache).
notes: user_activities is APPEND-ONLY in practice — there is no UI to edit or delete entries. Treat any 'delete an audit row' request as a red flag.
Volume scaling: a busy production tenant writes ~10k rows/day into user_activities. Always paginate; never request without a filter and limit.
If a write went through the legacy CakePHP UI (not the v5 API), it ALSO writes a user_activities row (POCOR-9697 ported the trait). Same redaction rules apply.

Pre-5.10.0 (i.e. Core <= 5.9) had per-row UserActivityLog::add() at scattered call sites — the new pattern is uniform via the model trait. If a row predates 2026-05 it may have a different shape (no per-field snapshot, only a free-text description).

playbooks.title: View a class's roster (institution-classes + students)
playbooks.description: Pull the students in a specific institution class. /api/v5/institution-classes (Core 5.10.0) is the class definition; institution-class-students joins it to the student roster. Webhook-enabled (POCOR-9257) — changes fire created/updated/deleted events.
schema_invariants: institution_classes fields: id, name, class_number, capacity, total_male_students, total_female_students, staff_id (homeroom teacher), institution_shift_id, institution_id, institution_unit_id, institution_course_id, academic_period_id.

total_male_students and total_female_students are CACHED counts updated by the application — they may briefly drift from the actual count in institution-class-students. Treat them as 'approximate' and verify with a count(institution-class-students) when accuracy matters.
Capacity is a soft limit — the API does NOT enforce it on enrolment. UI may warn; backend will accept.
POCOR-9257 webhooks: created / updated / deleted events for institution-classes are dispatched on each write. Useful for downstream sync but irrelevant to read paths.
steps: Identify the class: openemis_get('institution-classes', params: {institution_id: <id>, academic_period_id: <period>, _fields: ['id','name','staff_id','institution_unit_id','capacity'], limit: 100}). Filter by name or institution_unit_id (the grade) as needed.

Get the roster: openemis_get('institution-class-students', params: {institution_class_id: <class_id>, _fields: ['student_id','education_grade_id','student_status_id','start_date','end_date'], limit: 200})

Resolve student details: openemis_get('institution-students', params: {ids: [<student_ids>], _fields: ['student_id','first_name','last_name','date_of_birth','gender_id']}). The ids= fan-out (v0.3.0+) lets you fetch many at once.
Resolve homeroom teacher: openemis_get('security-users', params: {id: <staff_id>, _fields: ['first_name','last_name','openemis_no']}). Only one lookup needed for the staff_id from step 1.

Render: class name + grade + capacity + roster (student#, name, status). Flag any student_status_id that's not Enrolled (e.g., Withdrawn, Transferred) since those students appear in the roster but are not active.
notes: institution-class-students has student-level status (student_status_id), not class-level. A withdrawn student stays in the roster as a historical record — UIs typically filter by student_status_id=1 (Enrolled) for the 'current' view.

POCOR-9687 changed how Enrolled (Repeater) is derived. If a student is in the roster of the same class for a second academic period, that's the repeater flow — handled by application logic, not a schema change.
If the homeroom teacher (staff_id) is null, the class has no assigned homeroom — common in early planning before staff assignments.

playbooks.title: Set / update a school accreditation (POCOR-9610, pro-only write)
playbooks.description: Create or update an institution_accreditations row via the v5 API. Available only in the pro distribution (free is read-only). Permission gate: caller's security role must have order < 5.
schema_invariants: POST body shape: { institution_id, education_programme_id, valid_from (YYYY-MM-DD), valid_to (YYYY-MM-DD or null) }. modified_user_id, created_user_id, modified, created are derived server-side from the JWT subject — DO NOT include them in the body (they are silently stripped by POCOR-9697).
valid_from is required. valid_to nullable (open-ended). Date format is YYYY-MM-DD; ISO datetime is also accepted and truncated.
Same row can be reused across years by updating valid_to to null when extending, or by POSTing a NEW row with a fresh valid_from when re-accredited after expiry.
steps: Verify the caller has write permission (role.order < 5). If unsure, dispatch a single openemis_get('institution-accreditations', params:{limit:1, institution_id:<id>}) and try the write — a 403 is the gate failing.

Resolve education_programme_id: openemis_get('education-programmes', params: {_fields:['id','code','name','education_cycle_id'], limit: 200}). Pick the programme the institution is being accredited for.
openemis_create('institution-accreditations', body: { institution_id, education_programme_id, valid_from: '2026-09-01', valid_to: '2030-08-31' })
On success the API returns the row with its assigned id. The audit trail (user_activities, POCOR-9697) records the CREATE with per-field snapshots — no separate audit call needed.

To EXTEND an existing accreditation: openemis_update('institution-accreditations', id: <accreditation_id>, body: { valid_to: '<new-date>' or null }). To REPLACE: POST a fresh row instead of updating valid_from.
notes: Permission errors return 403 with a 'Forbidden' message. There is no special UNAUTHORIZED-because-of-role-order shape — same code as 'JWT missing or invalid'. Distinguish by checking the bearer is present and valid.

Do NOT include education_programme_id values from inactive education_systems / education_levels — there is no FK constraint catching this, the write will succeed but the row will be invisible in the Institution → Accreditations UI.
There is no soft-delete. openemis_delete is irreversible. POCOR-9697 captures the deletion in user_activities for forensic recovery — but the row itself is gone.

playbooks.title: Set / update a school registration (POCOR-9610, pro-only write)
playbooks.description: Create or update an institution_registrations row. Sibling of set-school-accreditation but simpler: there is no programme link, only the institution and the valid_from..valid_to window.
schema_invariants: POST body shape: { institution_id, valid_from (YYYY-MM-DD), valid_to (YYYY-MM-DD or null) }. Same server-side derivation of audit fields.

An institution typically has one Active registration row at a time. The API does NOT enforce non-overlap — it is policy-level. The application UI sorts by valid_from DESC and treats the newest Active row as 'current'.
steps: openemis_get('institution-registrations', params: {institution_id: <id>, orderby:'valid_from', order:'desc'}) — review existing rows to decide CREATE vs UPDATE.
If extending: openemis_update('institution-registrations', id:<existing_id>, body:{valid_to:'<new-date>' or null})
If new registration cycle: openemis_create('institution-registrations', body:{institution_id, valid_from:'YYYY-MM-DD', valid_to:'YYYY-MM-DD' or null})
Confirm by re-listing — newest row should be Active.
notes: Same role.order < 5 write gate as accreditations. Same audit shape (user_activities CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE per POCOR-9697).
If valid_from is set in the future, the registration is in Future state — the UI will show it but it's not yet in force.

playbooks.title: Mark student meal participation (pro-only write)
playbooks.description: Write per-day meal participation into student_meal_marked_records. Used during meal-distribution roll call: which students received which benefit on a given date. Free MCP only reads this (via view-institution-meals); writes are pro-only.
schema_invariants: student_meal_marked_records columns: id, institution_id, academic_period_id, institution_class_id, meal_programmes_id, date, meal_benefit_id. Note the column is meal_programmes_id (with an S, pointing at meal_programmes), not meal_programme_id.

One row per (student in class, programme, date, benefit). The same student CAN have multiple rows on the same date if they receive multiple benefits — no unique constraint enforces 'one per student per day'.
date is YYYY-MM-DD. Use the institution's local date, not server UTC.
steps: Identify which class and programme: openemis_get('meal-institution-programmes', params:{institution_id:<id>, academic_period_id:<period>}) — this gives you the meal_programme_id (the underlying programme id) and meal_implementer_id.
Resolve which students are in the class today: openemis_get('institution-class-students', params:{institution_class_id:<class>, student_status_id:1, _fields:['student_id']}).

For each student you want to mark, POST: openemis_create('student-meal-marked-records', body:{institution_id, academic_period_id, institution_class_id, meal_programmes_id, date:'YYYY-MM-DD', meal_benefit_id}).
Absence-by-omission: if a student is in the class today but does NOT get a row, they did not receive a meal. The application uses this convention rather than null entries.
Confirm by re-reading: openemis_get('student-meal-marked-records', params:{institution_class_id:<class>, date:'YYYY-MM-DD', _fields:['student_id','meal_benefit_id']}).
notes: There is no v5 endpoint that bulk-marks 'everyone present today.' Loop POSTs, or build the array client-side and submit one-by-one.

Mistakes are corrected via openemis_delete on the row, not by overwriting. The composite of (student_id implied by class roster, date, meal_benefit_id) is not enforced as unique, so an overwrite would create a duplicate.

playbooks.title: View a future student's admission / enrolment queue state
playbooks.description: Answer 'where is this child in the admission process?' and 'have they been enrolled yet?'. OpenEMIS routes new students through TWO sequential workflows: first the admission application (institution-student-admission), then enrolment (institution-student-enrolment). Each record carries a status_id that points at a workflow_step (e.g., 'Pending Verification', 'Approved', 'Closed'), an assignee_id (the staff member currently responsible), and a full audit trail in workflow-transitions / workflow-comments. This playbook reads — never writes — those records to surface the queue state in plain language.
playbooks.why_workflows: OpenEMIS treats admission and enrolment as multi-step approval processes because schools across countries have very different sign-off chains. A village school may need only the principal's tick; a national education ministry may require district verification, headmaster review, and registrar approval. The workflow plugin lets each tenant configure the steps, the role-based assignees, and the rules (e.g., 'auto-reject if days_unmarked > 5') without code changes. State machine enforcement is what stops an applicant from being marked Enrolled before the Admission row has been Approved.
schema_invariants: institution-student-admission columns: id, start_date, end_date, student_id, status_id, assignee_id, institution_id, academic_period_id, education_grade_id, institution_class_id, test_score, interview_score, comment.
institution-student-enrolment columns: id, start_date, end_date, student_id, status_id, assignee_id, institution_id, academic_period_id, education_grade_id, institution_class_id, comment.

status_id is a FK into workflow_statuses (the legacy compatibility layer). The actual workflow position lives in workflow_steps via the workflow_statuses_steps join table. workflow_steps.category maps 1=TO_DO, 2=IN_PROGRESS, 3=DONE — this tells you whether the record is 'queued', 'being worked on', or 'finished'.
assignee_id is a FK to security_users — the person currently responsible. If null, the record is unassigned and waiting for triage.

Every transition (status_id change, assignee change, comment) is logged in workflow-transitions with prev_workflow_step_name + workflow_step_name + workflow_action_name (typically APPROVE or REJECT). Joined to the originating row by (workflow_model_id, model_reference).
workflow-comments stores free-text comments left during transitions, joined to the model row the same way.
Admission MUST close before enrolment opens. A student can only have one Admission record per (institution_id, academic_period_id, education_grade_id) tuple in IN_PROGRESS state at a time.

steps.title: Resolve the student
steps.purpose: Find the security_users.id given a name or openemis_no. Required to scope the admission/enrolment lookup.
steps.guidance: Filter by openemis_no:<no> if you have it, else first_name + last_name. Capture the resolved id as student_id (NOTE: institution-students.student_id is the FK to security_users.id, not a separate 'student' table id).

steps.title: Find the latest admission record
steps.purpose: Pull the admission application(s) for this student.
steps.guidance: Filter student_id:<id>. If multiple rows (re-applications), order by created DESC and take the most recent. Note the status_id, assignee_id, education_grade_id, and institution_id values for the next steps.

steps.title: Resolve the admission's workflow step name
steps.purpose: Find which workflow_model represents InstitutionStudentAdmission so we can fetch the right workflow definition.
steps.guidance: Filter by model:'Institution.InstitutionStudentAdmissions' (or grep for 'StudentAdmission' in the name field). Note the returned id — call it admission_workflow_model_id.

steps.title: Map status_id → workflow_step → human label
steps.purpose: Join the admission's status_id to its underlying workflow_step.
steps.guidance: Filter workflow_status_id:<admission.status_id>. The row gives you the workflow_step_id. Then GET workflow-steps/{workflow_step_id} to read name (e.g., 'Pending Verification') and category (1/2/3 → TO_DO / IN_PROGRESS / DONE).

steps.title: Resolve the current assignee
steps.purpose: If assignee_id is not null, fetch the staff member's name so the answer reads naturally.
steps.guidance: Single-record GET on security-users/{assignee_id} with _fields:['first_name','last_name','openemis_no']. Skip if assignee_id is null (admission row is unassigned).

steps.title: Read the transition history
steps.purpose: Build a timeline of how the admission moved through steps.
steps.guidance: Filter workflow_model_id:<admission_workflow_model_id> AND model_reference:<admission.id>. Order by created DESC. Each row records prev_workflow_step_name → workflow_step_name with the action (APPROVE/REJECT) and the actor (created_user_id). This is the audit trail to surface to the user.

steps.title: If admission is DONE (category=3), check enrolment
steps.purpose: Once admission is approved (Closed), enrolment becomes the next workflow. Fetch the enrolment row.
steps.guidance: Filter student_id:<id>, institution_id:<id>, academic_period_id:<id>. Repeat steps 3-6 against the enrolment workflow_model (typically model:'Institution.StudentUser' or similar — find via workflow-models). If enrolment is also category=3, the student is fully enrolled.

steps.title: Render in plain language
steps.purpose: Produce a paragraph the user can understand.
steps.guidance: Example output: 'Anna Hassan applied to Avory Primary on 2026-04-12. Her admission is currently at step "Pending Verification" (TO_DO), assigned to Mr Ravi Kumar. The application has moved through 2 transitions: Submitted → Under Review (Apr 13, by Ms Aaisha) → Pending Verification (Apr 15, by Ms Aaisha). She has NOT been enrolled yet — enrolment opens only after admission is approved.'

notes: Workflow-controlled writes (approving admission, rejecting, reassigning) cannot be driven via this MCP — they require human approval and use the Workflow plugin's processWorkflow component. The free MCP is read-only by design; the pro MCP defers workflow writes to the OpenEMIS application per the workflow_writes_deferred_to_app global policy. Do not attempt to POST to /api/v5/institution-student-admission to 'approve' a record.

If status_id matches a workflow_step with category=3 (DONE) but workflow_step.name is 'Closed - Rejected' (not 'Closed - Approved'), the applicant was rejected — they will NOT proceed to enrolment. Surface that clearly.

The legacy status_id values like 'submitted' / 'under_review' you may see in older test data are kept for backward compatibility via workflow_statuses. Modern installations use numeric workflow_step_ids — both shapes appear in the wild.

playbooks.title: Explain the OpenEMIS workflow system (admissions, enrolment, leave, transfer)
playbooks.description: Educational playbook — answer 'why does this approval take 4 steps?', 'what is a workflow step vs. a workflow status?', 'who can approve this?'. OpenEMIS uses the Workflow plugin to model every multi-step approval (student admission, student enrolment, staff leave, staff/student transfer, training applications). This playbook explains the concepts so a user can read the database and figure out why a record is stuck.
playbooks.why_workflows: Schools differ wildly in how they approve things. A small private kindergarten may approve a student's admission with one principal's tick; a country's national education ministry may need: registrar verification → school principal review → district inspection → MOE final stamp. Hard-coding that chain in PHP would require a code release every time a country changes its process. The Workflow plugin makes the chain DATA, not CODE — admins configure steps, role-based assignees, transitions, and rules through the UI, and the same engine powers every domain that needs approvals.

concepts.name: workflow_models
concepts.meaning: The registry of domain models that the workflow engine can govern (e.g., 'Institution.InstitutionStudentAdmissions', 'Institution.StaffLeave'). Adding a new domain to workflow means writing a row here and attaching WorkflowBehavior to that model.

concepts.name: workflows
concepts.meaning: A named approval template bound to a workflow_model. One workflow_model can have many workflows (e.g., 'Standard Admission' vs. 'Boarding-school Admission'). Each tenant configures their own.

concepts.name: workflow_steps
concepts.meaning: Discrete stages within a workflow. Each step has a category — 1=TO_DO (queued), 2=IN_PROGRESS (being worked on), 3=DONE (closed). Saving a workflow auto-creates the three system steps Open / Pending / Closed; admins add more (e.g., 'Pending Verification', 'Pending Principal Approval').

concepts.name: workflow_actions
concepts.meaning: Transitions between steps. Each action has a source step, a target step, and a verb (action=0 APPROVE, 1=REJECT). The state machine BLOCKS any status change that isn't a defined workflow_action — that's how the plugin enforces 'you cannot skip the principal'.

concepts.name: workflow_steps_roles
concepts.meaning: Which security_roles are authorized to act on a given step. Restricts WHO can approve/reject at each stage. Example: 'Pending Principal Approval' is restricted to roles where role.name='Principal'.

concepts.name: workflow_statuses + workflow_statuses_steps
concepts.meaning: Legacy compatibility layer. Older domain models store status_id pointing at workflow_statuses; the join table maps that to the modern workflow_step_id. Both still work — newer installs increasingly skip the legacy layer.

concepts.name: workflow_transitions
concepts.meaning: Audit trail. Every time a record moves between steps (or its assignee changes, or an admin comments), one row is appended here. Read this to answer 'who approved, when, and why?'.

concepts.name: workflow_comments
concepts.meaning: Free-text comments left during transitions — typically the reason for rejection, or notes from the reviewer. Joined to the source record by (workflow_model_id, model_reference).

concepts.name: assignee_id (on the source row, NOT on workflow-*)
concepts.meaning: The current handler. When a record advances to a step like 'Pending Principal Approval', the system pushes the row into the principal's queue by setting assignee_id to the principal's security_users.id. UI dashboards filter by assignee_id = current_user to show 'tasks waiting on me'.

concepts.name: workflow_rules
concepts.meaning: JSON-encoded conditional triggers. Example: 'auto-reject staff leave if days_unmarked > 5'. The rule fires on specific events and can transition the workflow without a human action. Powerful for automation; rare in vanilla tenants.

steps: openemis_get('workflow-models', params:{_fields:['id','name','model'], limit:50}) — see every domain governed by workflow
For any specific domain (e.g., admissions): openemis_get('workflows', params:{workflow_model_id:<id>, _fields:['id','code','name']}) — see which workflow templates are configured
openemis_get('workflow-steps', params:{workflow_id:<id>, _fields:['id','name','category']}) — see the stages in that template, ordered by category
openemis_get('workflow-actions', params:{workflow_step_id:<step_id>, _fields:['id','name','next_workflow_step_id','action']}) — see which transitions are allowed FROM a given step
openemis_get('workflow-steps-roles', params:{workflow_step_id:<step_id>}) joined with security-roles to see WHO can act on a given step
openemis_get('workflow-transitions', params:{workflow_model_id:<id>, model_reference:<row_id>, orderby:'created', order:'desc'}) — audit trail for a specific record
notes: WHY THE PLUGIN EXISTS: configurability. The same PHP code powers admission approval in a 30-student village school in Mongolia and a 5,000-student urban academy in Brazil — they just configure different steps, roles, and rules.

THE THREE SYSTEM STEPS (Open, Pending, Closed) are auto-created with every new workflow and CANNOT be deleted (is_system_defined=1). They guarantee that every workflow has a sensible entry and exit point.

The plugin EXPLICITLY DOES NOT allow agents (this MCP included) to drive transitions. Workflow-controlled writes require the human-in-the-loop approval chain — see [[mark-student-attendance]] for an example of a workflow-controlled write that we deliberately defer to the OpenEMIS UI.
